summary: Intermittent VPN/DNS failures to private deployment test environment
description: Issue summary: Engineers intermittently cannot reach internal private deployment test hosts over VPN from remote office and home networks. Failures present as DNS resolution timeouts or long tail connection drops to internal staging endpoints (10.240.x.x) used for on-call tests. Impact: Blocking some end-to-end tests and manual QA for private deployment workflows; intermittent but reproducible during high-traffic windows. Environment: staging - us-east; private deployment cluster (on-prem lab) reachable via corporate VPN. Steps to reproduce: 1) Connect to corporate VPN from a remote laptop (home WiFi or office guest). 2) Attempt curl https://staging-private.internal.redwood: read timeout ~10s observed or "could not resolve host". 3) Retry; sometimes succeeds after 30-90s. Logs / observations: - Several clients show DNS NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL at time of failure. - Local resolver on VPN gateway shows elevated query latency. - Some traceroutes reveal packet loss between VPN gateway and internal DNS cluster during incidents. - SRE run: dig +trace for staging-private.internal returned inconsistent NS responses during window. Hypothesis: Either DNS caching/TTL misconfiguration on VPN edge or intermittent packet loss causing DNS lookups to fail and fall back slowly; possible overloaded edge NAT/firewall sessions causing packet drops. Workarounds tried: - Added static /etc/hosts entry on a single test runner to bypass DNS — connectivity stable for that host. - Restarted VPN-gateway resolver process (temporary improvement for ~2 hours). Next steps: - SRE (Priya) to capture pcap around failure window on VPN gateway and internal DNS servers. - Network team to inspect edge firewall/NAT session counts during incidents. - Consider reducing DNS TTL and adding additional resolver pool behind load balancer. - Add monitoring alert for elevated DNS query latency and query failure rate.
